title: Private deployments: cost scenarios & licensing bundles (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is an early draft of comparative cost scenarios and recommended packaging for Private deployments (on-prem vs VPC). Goal: short, actionable guidance for GTM and sales engineering on pricing anchors and tradeoffs + a sensitivity matrix for typical customer profiles (small, mid, enterprise).

Scope / audience:
- Audience: sales engineering, pricing, product, solutions engineering.
- Scope: 36-month TCO comparison for three archetypes; line-item breakout (HW, infra ops, network, software license, support, infra depreciation, facilities for on-prem).
- Not included: professional services upsell (handled separately), lead-time / procurement risk modeling (TODO).

Assumptions (base case unless noted):
- Time horizon: 3 years (36 months).
- Model sizes supported: 70B and 13B families. Baseline load: 200 QPS inference-equivalent across 8-hour business curve, peak factor 2.
- On-prem hardware unit: 4x A100-80GB equivalent per cluster node. Unit cost (capex) = $320k per node (incl. rack, switch amortized install) in base.
- VPC host cost: equivalent reserved instance blended price $11.5k/month per node (includes GPU/USD + instance overhead).
- Network (egress + private circuits): on-prem internal networking $1.5k/mo, VPC cross-region egress averaged $2.1k/mo for this load case.
- Support tiers: Essentials (8x5 email, ticket triage), Enterprise (24x7 phone + critical SLAs), Premium (dedicated TAM + on-call rotation). Licenses priced as % of base software value.
- Software license baseline: $40k/month for a committed private control plane instance (covers control plane, metrics retention, standard rollout features). Price scales by model count and high-availability topology.
- Support addons: Essentials = 15% of license/year, Enterprise = 30% license/year, Premium = 55% license/year + per-seat TAM.
- Discounting: none applied in scenarios (present-value not used) — simple cash-flow comparison.

Base-case 3-year summary (rounded):
- Small customer (pilot): on-prem = $890k total, VPC = $615k total.
- Mid customer (production): on-prem = $3.8M total, VPC = $2.6M total.
- Enterprise (regulated, multi-region): on-prem = $11.6M total, VPC = $9.9M total (note: on-prem often higher because of HA and facilities).

Key line-item differences (explanation):
- CapEx vs OpEx: on-prem frontloads HW purchases (Year 0–1) whereas VPC spreads GPU spend monthly. On-prem shows faster IRR for multi-year, high-utilization cases but requires capital and procurement lead time.
- Support as a % of license: enterprises value SLA and TAM — high support tiers significantly change TCO when added as annual charges.
- Licensing model shape: flat monthly license vs per-node seat pricing; flat license preferred for customers with bursty usage because it decouples cost from peak spikes.

Detailed sensitivity notes (high level):
- HW price variance +/- 20%: on-prem 3yr TCO swings +/- 12% for mid customer.
- Utilization variance (60% -> 100%): on-prem per-token cost drops materially at >85% utilization; VPC marginal cost remains linear.
- Support tier selection: moving from Essentials -> Enterprise adds ~20% to 3yr spend for mid customer but reduces time-to-resolution and risk for high-SLA apps.

Packaging & recommendation ideas (draft):
- License packaging (3 tiers):
  1) Private Essentials: control plane + basic telemetry, single-region, Essentials support. Recommended for pilots/proof-of-concept. Pricing: smaller fixed monthly license + optional per-node add-on.
  2) Private Standard: HA control plane, model pinning, rollout features, Enterprise support optional. Pricing: higher baseline license that includes single failover region.
  3) Private Enterprise: multi-region control plane, advanced rollback/automatic fallback, enterprise SLAs, TAM + audit/compliance bundle. Pricing: premium license + mandatory Enterprise or Premium support.
- Financing flow: offer 12–24 month hardware financing for on-prem to reduce sticker shock; include an option to convert to VPC credits if customer migrates within 36 months.
- Discount patterns: normalize discounts as either license % off for committed reserved GPU spend or flat $/node credits. Always tie deep discounts to multi-year capacity commitments and a minimum support tier.

Sales engineering talking points (concise):
- If customer expects >85% sustained GPU utilization and has capital available, on-prem with financing can beat VPC on raw unit economics over 36 months.
- If customer needs rapid scale, lower procurement risk, or limited ops headcount, VPC will be cheaper and operationally simpler.
- For regulated customers, private control plane + Enterprise support is frequently non-negotiable. Ensure SLAs and KMS/HSM options are clearly priced.

Open questions / TODO (action items):
- [PROD-4821] Confirm up-to-date vendor HW pricing (2026 quotes) and update base node cost (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-03-10).
- Validate blended VPC reserved pricing across AWS/GCP/Azure for regions (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-17).
- Build an interactive sheet (separate file) to allow SEs to plug customer-specific inputs (QPS, models, utilization, HA requirements). Samir to own template.

Risk notes:
- Procurement lead time for on-prem (12–20 weeks) can cause missed revenue windows — include expected lead-time discounts/offers for customers willing to wait.
- Depreciation assumptions and refresh cycles: 36 months chosen as default; for customers with 48–60 month cycles, on-prem economics weaken vs VPC.

Suggested next steps (immediate):
1) Convert this draft into an interactive Google Sheet that exposes key knobs (HW cost, utilization, support tier) with prefilled archetype presets. (Owner: Samir, ETA: 2026-03-05)
2) Draft a short one-pager for GTM with 3 pre-baked scenarios and recommended onboarding offers (Owner: Aisha, ETA: 2026-03-09).
3) Review packaging language with Legal (contractual terms for TAM, SLA credits, migration credits) (Owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-18).

Notes to self / SE scratchpad (informal):
- Consider an "on-prem pilot kit" offer: 6-month pilot license + 50% hardware financing and 30% credit toward first-year license if they convert to enterprise.
- Watch out for customers that insist on per-node licensing — that interacts badly with autoscaling/burst models. Prefer flat license with node add-ons.
- Keep a simple rule-of-thumb: if customer wants private for compliance and will run <30% utilization, recommend VPC + private control plane instead of full on-prem.

Version notes: this is a working draft — expect numbers to shift after vendor quotes and region-specific VPC blends. Please comment inline, flag anything that should be moved to a final GTM playbook.
